verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.72 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 74.2, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: AP 16. The twin of 74.1, but the two inverses are of DIFFERENT functions and the target is a Cos⁻¹ — so the cosine addition formula is used, and its middle sign is a MINUS. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print 1+1+1+1 against answer 77 on book p.73, so the shape is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow it. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. ONE PRESENTATION CHOICE, made deliberately: the book draws a small right triangle beside each answer that needs a second ratio (for example sinα = 4/5 giving cosα = 3/5). Those are authored here as the one-line algebraic step instead, with the triangle route named in the margin note — it keeps the nine answers consistent and avoids three near-identical figures where the algebra is a single line. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q16 is the Inverse Trig Functions slot. NOTE: Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-ONLY unit — the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot, and this book has no Inverse Trig LAQ chapter (LAQ chapters are 1-6) and no VSAQ chapter (VSAQ chapters are 14-19). The same shape as Unit 7. Verified by walking to p.75, where SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles begins.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Name the angles and find their other ratios
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. One angle arrives by its sine, the other by its cosine — so the missing ratio is found the other way round in each case. Both are 3-4-5 style triangles.
steps.memory_tip: One angle arrives by its sine, the other by its cosine, so the missing ratio is found the other way round each time.
lines: Take Sin⁻¹(3/5) = α and Cos⁻¹(12/13) = β
RTP: α + β = Cos⁻¹(33/65), that is, cos(α+β) = 33/65

recall.must_convey: That both inverses are named as angles and all four ratios found: sinα = 3/5, cosα = 4/5, cosβ = 12/13, sinβ = 5/13.
accept: name them alpha and beta, one gives the sine and the other the cosine, then find the missing ratios
sin alpha is three fifths so cos alpha is four fifths, cos beta is twelve thirteenths so sin beta is five thirteenths
get all four ratios from the two triangles
rendintini angles ga peru petti, naalugu ratios kanukovali
find the other ratio for each angle

steps.why: The cosine addition formula needs both sines AND both cosines, so all four ratios have to exist before it can be applied.
common_mistakes: Assuming the second inverse is also a sine.
Getting sinβ = 12/13 by reading the wrong side.

steps.label: Apply the cos(A+B) formula
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The target is a Cos⁻¹, so the cosine formula is the one to use — and note the MINUS between the two products, where the sine formula had a plus.
steps.memory_tip: The target is a Cos⁻¹, so use cos(A + B) — with a MINUS between the two products.
lines: cos(α + β) = cosα cosβ − sinα sinβ

recall.must_convey: That cos(α+β) = cosα cosβ − sinα sinβ is applied, giving 33/65.
accept: use cos A plus B equals cos A cos B minus sin A sin B to get thirty three over sixty five
apply the cosine addition formula with the minus sign
forty eight over sixty five minus fifteen over sixty five is thirty three over sixty five
cos alpha cos beta minus sin alpha sin beta apply cheyyali
the cosine of the sum is thirty three by sixty five

steps.why: cos(A+B) carries a minus where sin(A+B) carries a plus. Putting a plus between the two products gives 48/65 + 15/65 = 63/65, which is cos(α − β), not cos(α + β).
common_mistakes: Using a plus between the two products.
Using the sine addition formula because the first inverse was a sine.

steps.label: Convert back to an inverse
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos(α+β) = 33/65 means α+β = Cos⁻¹(33/65).
steps.memory_tip: cos(α + β) = 33/65 means α + β = Cos⁻¹(33/65), not Sin⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That cos(α+β) = 33/65 is converted back to α + β = Cos⁻¹(33/65).
accept: since the cosine of the sum is thirty three over sixty five the sum is cos inverse of that
convert back to cos inverse form
alpha plus beta is cos inverse thirty three by sixty five
cos value nunchi cos inverse ki marchali
write the result in inverse form

steps.why: Which inverse function appears in the answer is decided by which compound formula was used — the cosine formula here gives a Cos⁻¹ answer, while the sine formula would give a Sin⁻¹ one.

insider_note: The target is a Cos⁻¹, so build cos(α + β) and stay with sines and cosines rather than tangents. The two angles give 3-4-5 and 5-12-13 triangles, so every ratio is exact.
